display.purpose: The single h1; the key phrase set in Solve Ink. Fixed at 1.9rem under 760px.

title.purpose: Station h3s with a numbered ink tag; terminal h3s step up to 1.6rem in their line's text colour.

lede.purpose: The one paragraph under the h1, 46ch; 0.98rem / 1.45 under 760px.

body.purpose: All prose at a 46ch measure; 500 for the status board's first column, 600 for the who phrase.

caption.purpose: Figcaptions (0.85rem), fine print and footer (0.9–0.95rem) in Muted Ink.

label.purpose: The nameplate and the table head: uppercase display face at 0.8rem with 0.06em tracking.

shadows.name: interchange-lift
shadows.purpose: The interchange only; the one surface that lies over the map.

motion.name: draw
motion.purpose: Lines draw themselves on load (stroke-dashoffset 1 → 0 with pathLength=1); staggered 0.15s, 0.3s, 0.9s; the dashed line animates to its --dash pattern.

motion.name: arrive
motion.purpose: Diagram labels and stations fade in after the lines.

motion.name: station-lit
motion.purpose: A route station fills with ink when its stop enters view (IntersectionObserver, rootMargin -30% bottom).

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Under prefers-reduced-motion everything is drawn and still; scroll-behavior auto.

strokes.name: line
strokes.value: stroke-width: 10 (SVG units); stroke-linecap: round; stroke-linejoin: round
strokes.purpose: Every line in the diagram; the CSS route bar is 10px with 5px corners.

strokes.name: line-planned
strokes.value: stroke-dasharray: var(--dash); --dash: 0.03 0.022 (desktop paths), 0.12 0.09 (mobile paths), in pathLength=1 units
strokes.purpose: The Contribute line; dashed means planned.

strokes.name: station
strokes.value: 20px disc, fill paper, 4px ink ring; lit = ink fill
strokes.purpose: Stations in the SVG (r=10, stroke 4) and in the CSS route.

strokes.name: section-rule
strokes.purpose: Header bottom, terminal separators, footer top, board and screenshot borders.

strokes.name: table-rule

narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Line Map"**

Gloki's landing page is a transit diagram, not a brochure. The ground is white paper; everything on it is either a line, a station, or a nameplate. Three coloured lines are the three ways in (Solve, Build, Contribute); they run straight or at 45°, cross a pale blue zone band, and meet at one interchange, which is the reader, holding the only form on the page. The system borrows Beck's discipline (a fixed stroke, round caps, black-ringed white stations, uppercase plates) and nothing else of his: the roundel is the brand mark's cousin, never a TfL copy.

The tone is plain and literal. Headings are a single rounded humanist display face at one weight; body copy is a quiet humanist sans held to a 46-character measure; colour appears only where it means something (a line, its plate, a status). Density is low and the rhythm is editorial: more air above a heading than below it, one idea per station. Depth is almost absent; the one shadow on the page belongs to the interchange and nothing else.

Confirmed rejections, from the build and from PRODUCT.md: no hero-plus-three-cards, no device mockup, no stock photography, no hype words, and no brand blue behind or inside body-size text.
keyCharacteristics: White paper, black ink, three line colours, one pale wash: the whole palette.
A 10-unit round-capped stroke is the line; a 20px white disc with a 4px ink ring is the station.
The nameplate (black bar, white uppercase display type, 2px corners) labels every control.
Dashed stroke means a planned line; the dash is the honesty marker, not decoration.
One authored moment: the lines draw themselves on load, then stations light as they enter view.

rules.name: The Stroke-Not-Text Rule
rules.body: `solve` (#3b82f6) and `contribute` (#d97706) are strokes and swatches only. Any character set in a line's colour uses that line's `-text` value, and no body-size text is ever white on brand blue.

rules.name: The Two-Value Line Rule
rules.body: Every line colour exists as a pair: a stroke value for the diagram and a text value for words and plates. Adding a line means adding both and checking both against paper and wash.

rules.name: The One Wash Rule
rules.body: Tinted ground is one pale blue, used for zone bands and alternating sections; there is no second tint and no grey.

rules.name: The One Weight Rule
rules.body: Hammersmith One ships at 400 only; hierarchy comes from size and the plate, never from weight.

rules.name: The 46ch Rule
rules.body: Prose never runs wider than 46 characters; the diagram, not the paragraph, is what spans the viewport.

rules.name: The Ink-Rule Rule
rules.body: Separation is a black rule, never a shadow or a grey line. The interchange is the one surface allowed to float, because it is the one surface that lies over the map.

dos: **Do** draw with the line grammar: 10-unit round-capped strokes, straight or at 45°, 20px stations with a 4px ink ring, and a nameplate for every label.
**Do** use the dashed stroke (18/14, or the repeating-gradient swatch) for anything planned and not yet real; the dash is how the page tells the truth.
**Do** set every line's words in its `-text` value and check it against both paper and wash (AA, 4.5:1 or better).
**Do** hold prose to 46ch in Cabin 400 at 1.0625rem / 1.55, and keep all headings in Hammersmith One at 400.
**Do** separate with ink rules (3px between sections, 2px inside tables) and alternate paper and wash for section ground.
**Do** keep every target 44px or taller, the focus ring 3px Contribute Ink at 3px offset, and the h1 singular.
donts: **Don't** set text in `solve` (#3b82f6) or `contribute` (#d97706), and don't put white text on brand blue at body size; use `solve-text` and `contribute-text`.
**Don't** add a shadow to anything but the interchange; depth here is an ink rule.
**Don't** introduce a second tint, a grey rule, a gradient fill, or a bold weight of the display face.
**Don't** replace the diagram with cards, a device mockup, or photography; the map is the hero and the form sits inside it.
**Don't** copy TfL: no bar-and-circle roundel, no Johnston; the station ring and the plate are the whole borrowing.
